Drafts — implementation plan

outline

A concrete plugin and state-file structure for a writing system that keeps rules, stylometry, working documents, and learning authority separate.

Release boundary

Ship Drafts as a dedicated plugin with one owning skill. The first release learns from user-authorized evidence, resolves explicit writing rules and context-specific stylometry, drafts or edits through artifact-specific workflows, and preserves long-running document state.

Personal state lives in a Drafts-owned host namespace; project and report state lives under .agents/drafts/. Rules remain human-editable files. Stylometry remains derived evidence. Only explicit promotion turns a candidate rule into an active rule.

Not in the first release: automatic mailbox or chat ingestion, sending messages, background learning, cross-device synchronization, multi-user service infrastructure, or autonomous publication.

How the Every research shapes Drafts

Source idea Drafts contract Owning files
AI style guides Encode voice tensions, structure, signature moves, anti-patterns, annotated examples, and revision checks as inspectable rules and descriptive profiles—not one prompt. rules/, stylometry/, language.md, learning.md
Writing with AI Interview first, negotiate the outline, draft section by section, adjudicate independent critics, then run AI-pattern, mechanical, line, and personal-voice checks. long-form.md, editing.md, artifact brief.md, outline.md, draft.md, and checkpoints
After automation Keep the user as framer and final judge. Agents can record evidence and propose rules, but cannot silently activate them or infer current intent from historical writing. SKILL.md, state-contract.md, learning.md, learning-events.jsonl

Build sequence

  1. 1
    Establish contracts

    Create the plugin shell, ubiquitous language, state-root contract, schemas, and deterministic precedence rules.

  2. 2
    Build state core

    Implement rule packs, context profiles, evidence ledgers, working documents, checkpoints, and effective-rule resolution.

  3. 3
    Add writing workflows

    Support quick messages, email, voice editing, and long-form interview, outline, drafting, review, and finalization.

  4. 4
    Add learning

    Extract stylometry, record edit pairs, propose candidate rules, and require explicit promotion before activation.

  5. 5
    Evaluate and ship

    Prove state integrity, context routing, rule authority, voice match, content preservation, and plugin portability.

Shape of each plugin file

File Shape Responsibility
plugin.json Name, version, description, author, keywords, category, assets path, and skills path. Portable plugin identity and package entrypoints.
.codex-plugin/plugin.json Shared metadata plus repository, skill path, UI interface, capabilities, default prompt, brand color, icon, and logo. Codex marketplace and composer presentation.
.claude-plugin/plugin.json Minimal Claude manifest: name, version, description, author, keywords. Claude plugin discovery without duplicating runtime guidance.
assets/icon.png Small square raster icon. Compact composer and marketplace identity.
assets/logo.png Large raster logo. Expanded plugin identity.
SKILL.md Frontmatter with only name and triggering description; body contains the invariant contract, workflow router, state-loading order, approval boundary, and conditional reference links. Select the correct Drafts workflow and preserve the human framing and promotion gates. Detailed schemas and variants stay out.
agents/openai.yaml display_name, short_description, default_prompt, icon paths, brand color, and implicit-invocation policy. Human-facing skill metadata that remains synchronized with SKILL.md.
references/language.md Ubiquitous-language glossary plus the invariant distinction among rules, stylometry, current intent, workflow, evidence, and voice. Keep every workflow, schema, test, and user-facing explanation semantically consistent.
references/state-contract.md Personal, context, project, artifact, and session scopes; state roots; one-writer rule; precedence; overrides; recovery; versioning; retention boundaries. Define where state lives, which state is canonical, and how conflicts resolve.
references/schemas.md Field-level contracts for profile, context, rule, stylometry, evidence events, working documents, and checkpoints, with one minimal valid example each. Give people and scripts one inspectable schema vocabulary without duplicating validation code.
references/workflow-selection.md Decision table for short message, email, long-form development, voice edit, developmental edit, line edit, final check, and profile maintenance. Scale process depth to the artifact and load only the relevant workflow reference.
references/long-form.md Interview questions, readiness signal, negotiated-outline loop, section drafting, critic-panel protocol, human adjudication, and final checks. Encode the Every long-form process without turning it into autonomous authorship.
references/editing.md Separate contracts for voice edit, developmental edit, line edit, AI-pattern scrub, mechanical style check, and personal-voice read. Prevent structural, factual, and stylistic changes from being conflated or silently learned.
references/learning.md Evidence capture, sample attribution, edit-pair classification, stylometry rebuild, candidate-rule proposal, explicit promotion, rejection, retirement, and rollback. Make learning conservative, traceable, context-scoped, and reversible.
scripts/drafts_state.py One deterministic CLI with verbs such as init, validate, resolve, record, checkpoint, promote, and retire. Own all file mutation, schema validation, effective-rule resolution, append-only events, and checkpoint creation.
scripts/stylometry.py Pure extraction and aggregation functions plus a CLI for rebuilding a global baseline or one context profile from an explicit corpus. Measure interpretable features and uncertainty. It never creates or activates rules.
assets/state/profile.yaml Minimal personal-profile skeleton: schema version, profile ID, context index, active stylometry version, created and updated timestamps. Seed the host-level Drafts profile.
assets/state/context.yaml Context ID and name; channel, genre, audience, relationship, purpose, project, and document-stage dimensions; inheritance pointers. Seed reusable named context profiles.
assets/state/rule.md YAML fields for ID, action, force, scope, status, authority, provenance, timestamps, and supersession; Markdown sections for directive, rationale, exceptions, preferred example, and avoided example. Seed one human-editable rule file.
assets/state/artifact.yaml Artifact ID, type, context, current workflow stage, checkpoint pointer, external source pointer, and timestamps. Seed project-local working-document state.
.drafts/evals/evals.json Authored scenarios for messages, email, reports, context isolation, rule conflict, promotion, rejection, resumption, and recovery. Development-only behavioral coverage; excluded from the portable skill runtime.
tests/test_state.py Focused tests for initialization, schema validation, precedence, override, event append, checkpoint, promotion, retirement, and recovery. Prove deterministic state semantics.
tests/test_stylometry.py Fixture-driven tests for feature extraction, corpus identity, global aggregation, context isolation, uncertainty, and version changes. Prove measurements are reproducible and cannot mutate normative rules.
tests/fixtures/ Small attributed sample corpora, edit pairs, rule packs, context profiles, and expected resolved-state snapshots. Keep deterministic tests realistic without using private user writing.

Runtime file Shape and authority
profile.yaml Canonical personal index: profile identity, context IDs, and active stylometry version. Human-editable metadata; scripts validate updates.
contexts/<id>.yaml Named combination of structured context dimensions and inheritance. Canonical for routing.
rules/**/<id>.md One prescriptive rule per file. Canonical, human-editable, scope-aware, and governed by explicit promotion.
stylometry/**/*.yaml Derived distributions, sample counts, corpus digest, extractor version, uncertainty, and evidence references. Rebuildable; never normative.
samples/<id>.md + samples.jsonl Attributed sample content plus append-only metadata: author confidence, context, origin, representative or aspirational status, timestamps, and digest.
edit-pairs.jsonl Append-only before and after references, context, accepted time, and classified content, structural, factual, or stylistic differences.
learning-events.jsonl Append-only proposal, approval, rejection, promotion, retirement, and rebuild events with actor, evidence references, and timestamps.
history/stylometry/<version>.yaml Immutable profile snapshot produced whenever the corpus or extractor changes.
.agents/drafts/index.yaml Project-local artifact index with IDs, paths, current stages, and last checkpoint pointers.
brief.md Current purpose, audience, stakes, desired reader effect, required facts, sources, and non-goals. The user’s present frame.
state.yaml Artifact type, context, workflow stage, active checkpoint, open questions, source pointer, and timestamps.
outline.md Negotiated structure with section purpose, evidence obligations, status, and rejected beats.
draft.md Current local draft when no external document is authoritative. Section boundaries remain aligned with the outline.
decisions.jsonl Append-only structural, editorial, and critic-adjudication decisions so rejected directions do not recur.
checkpoints/<version>.md Immutable draft snapshot with parent, workflow stage, author, timestamp, and the state digest that produced it.

Contracts and proof

Surface Initial contract Proof boundary
Rules One file per rule; layered packs; visible inheritance, overrides, authority, force, and lifecycle. Schema fixtures plus precedence and conflict tests.
Stylometry Versioned global baseline and context profiles with corpus identity, distributions, and uncertainty. Deterministic extraction fixtures and context-isolation checks.
Documents Brief, current intent, outline, decisions, revisions, checkpoints, and recovery state remain artifact-scoped. Checkpoint, resume, fork, and stale-state scenarios.
Learning Authorized evidence may update stylometry or propose rules; promotion is explicit and traceable. Edit-pair classification, candidate lifecycle, rejection, promotion, and rollback tests.
Writing Current intent overrides durable preferences for the task; active rules outrank stylometric tendencies. Behavioral scenarios separately grade rule compliance, voice match, content preservation, and naturalness.

Delivery gate

The first release is ready when a user can initialize Drafts, add representative samples, inspect the derived profile, create or edit a rule, draft in at least two distinct contexts, resume a long-form document, and explicitly promote or reject a candidate rule without hidden state changes.

Validation should combine focused unit and fixture tests, Meta-Skill validation for the owning skill, authored behavioral evaluations, manifest consistency checks, and the repository-wide verification gate.

Implement Drafts vertically, beginning with contracts and one complete email workflow. Prove state initialization, rule resolution, context selection, drafting, edit-pair capture, and explicit promotion end to end before adding long-form reports or broader stylometry.

This keeps the first implementation reviewable while testing every architectural boundary that later workflows depend on.

Workflow basis: Every — AI Style Guides; After Automation; Writing With AI Is Harder Than You Think. Architecture basis: confirmed Drafts decision record and current Dots plugin conventions.
